hash32.does: one 32-bit integer, well mixed: inputs one bit apart give outputs about half their bits apart
tests: it gives the same values as the published C function, over 10,000 inputs
changing one input bit changes about half of the output bits (full avalanche)

fnv1a.does: a string as a 32-bit number: each character mixed in with an exclusive or, then a multiplication
tests: it gives the RFC's own test values for its four test strings

hashString.does: a string as a well-mixed 32-bit number: FNV-1a, then hash32 over it
hashString.notes: Chaining the two is this almanac's choice. When a seed name's last character moves by one (a1, a2), FNV-1a alone changes about 10 of the 32 bits, and as few as 5; hash32 over it brings that to about 16, half, as unrelated numbers would be.
tests: it is hash32 of fnv1a
seed names one character apart give numbers about half their bits apart, where FNV-1a alone gives fewer than a third

SeededRandom.does: numbers in [0, 1) from a seed: the same seed, the same sequence; with ranges, whole numbers, chances, signs and picks
SeededRandom.notes: The numbers are mulberry32's, its state kept to 32 bits (a JavaScript number would otherwise grow until it lost precision, some 5 million draws in). The seeding (a seed is hashed, mixed with the constant 0x9e3779b9 and never left at 0) is this almanac's own.
tests: its numbers are mulberry32's: they match the published C function for the same state
the same seed gives the same sequence, and a string seed gives the same sequence as its hash
every number is in [0, 1), and range, int, chance and pick give only what they are asked for
the numbers are spread evenly: over 100,000 draws each tenth of [0, 1) gets 10% of them, give or take 0.3%
its state stays a 32-bit integer, so after 6 million draws it still matches the published C function
sign gives -1 or 1, each about half the time

twoBoneLimb.does: a limb of two bones reaching for a point: where its middle joint goes so its tip lands on the point
twoBoneLimb.notes: Out of reach, the limb stops a hundredth of a unit short of straight (whatever the units), so its joint keeps bending the chosen way instead of locking; its tip then points a little off the point, by at most about 4/√L degrees for a limb L units long (under 3 degrees at 2 units, 1 degree at 16, less the longer it is).
tests: when the point is in reach, the tip lands on it
the bones keep their lengths
out of reach, the limb reaches toward the point, a hundredth short of straight, its joint still bent the chosen way
bend picks the side of the joint: -1 mirrors 1 across the line from the hip to the point
it changes nothing it is given, and the same input gives the same output

gaitTiming.does: which legs step together in a gait: the phase of each leg, pair by pair, front to back
gaitTiming.notes: In the bound, each fore leg lags the other by 0.4 (and each hind leg likewise): tuned by eye, not taken from a measurement.
tests: a trot moves diagonal legs together
a walk puts each of the four legs a quarter step from another
a bound moves the fore legs nearly together and the hind legs nearly together, half a step apart
a tripod moves three legs at a time: alternate legs on one side with the middle leg of the other
a wave starts each pair a quarter step before the pair in front of it, so the step travels from back to front
unknown gaits and wrong numbers of legs are refused with a message saying what is allowed
it gives a new table each time, so changing one changes no other

clamp.does: a number kept inside a range

with no range given, the range is 0 to 1

lerp.does: part of the way from one number to another, in a straight line

smoothstep.does: where a number is between two edges, eased so it starts and ends level

it starts and ends level, and never goes down on the way

wrap.does: a number wrapped round a span, never negative: what scrolls off one side comes back on the other
wrap.notes: JavaScript's % keeps the sign of the number (-30 % 100 is -30); wrap gives the remainder that is never negative (70), the one scrolling needs.
tests: the result is always 0 or more and less than the span, and differs from the number by whole spans

latticeRandom.does: a number in [0, 1) for each point of a grid and a seed: the random values value noise blends
latticeRandom.notes: The grid point and the seed are mixed by multiplying each by its own large odd number and hashing with hash32; the multipliers are this almanac's choice.
tests: the same grid point and seed give the same number, in [0, 1)
over a 100 by 100 grid, each tenth of [0, 1) gets 10% of the points, give or take 0.6%

valueNoise.does: smooth noise in 0..1 across the plane: a random number at each grid point, blended between them
valueNoise.notes: The blend between grid points is eased with 3t² - 2t³ (smoothstep), so the grid does not show as creases.
tests: at a grid point it is that point's lattice number
it stays within 0 to 1, and a small step moves it only a little

fractalNoise.does: noise with detail at every size: value noise at several scales, each finer one fainter
fractalNoise.notes: Each octave is read with its own seed (seed + 101 per octave), so the scales do not line up.
tests: with one octave it is value noise
it stays within 0 to 1, and more octaves add finer detail

ridgedNoise.does: noise whose highs are thin sharp lines: each scale of fractal noise folded at its middle
ridgedNoise.notes: This is the plain form: each octave folded, then summed, halving each time. Texturing and Modeling also gives a ridged multifractal, in which each octave is weighted by the one before; that is not done here.
tests: with one octave it is value noise folded at its middle, highest where the noise is a half
it stays within 0 to 1

noiseLine.does: value noise along a line: a number in 0..1 that wanders smoothly as x moves
noiseLine.notes: Reading the plane along a line chosen by the seed (y = 0.731 seed + 7.3) is this almanac's convenience: one-dimensional noise without a second implementation.
tests: it is value noise read along one line of the plane, a line for each seed

hexToRgb.does: a "#rrggbb" or "#rgb" colour as [red, green, blue]

nothing reads as middle grey

rgbToHex.does: [red, green, blue] as "#rrggbb", rounded and kept in range

rgba.does: [red, green, blue] and an opacity as a CSS colour for a canvas

mixColour.does: part of the way from one colour to another, channel by channel

shade.does: a colour darkened toward black or lightened toward white
tests: below 0 it moves toward black, above 0 toward white, by that share of the way

luma.does: how bright a colour looks, 0..1, weighing green most and blue least as the eye does

its weights are BT.601's: 0.299 red, 0.587 green, 0.114 blue

rgbToHsl.does: a colour as hue, saturation and lightness: the colour wheel's terms

hslToRgb.does: hue, saturation and lightness back to [red, green, blue]

aerialPerspective.does: a colour as the day shows it at a distance: faded toward the horizon the further it is, and dimmed after dark
aerialPerspective.notes: The fading never passes 92%, so even the furthest hills keep a trace of their own colour. The night's dimming is this almanac's own: after dark a colour moves (85% of the way at full night) toward a darker version of itself tinted by the top of the night sky, so things go dark and take the sky's hue.
tests: near and in full daylight, a colour is itself
the further away, the nearer it is to the horizon's colour, but never all the way
after dark a colour is dimmed

parallax.does: how far a layer scrolls when the camera moves: in proportion to how near it is
tests: a layer at the horizon never moves, the nearest moves with the camera, and one half way moves half as far

turnedProjection.does: a point of a turning grid to the screen: turned round the centre, tipped back to half its depth, lifted by its height
turnedProjection.notes: Games call this view isometric. With the ground tipped to half its depth (2:1 pixels, lines at about 26.6 degrees) it is, strictly, dimetric; true isometric draws those lines at 30 degrees.
tests: unturned, a tile is the scale wide and half the scale deep, and each level lifts a point by the lift
the grid's centre lands where it is told at every angle, and a quarter turn puts each corner where the next one was

turnedDepth.does: how far back a point of a turning grid is: draw the farthest first, so the near is painted over the far
tests: it orders points as the screen does: the greater depth is the lower point on the screen, nearer the viewer

flockStep.does: a flock or a school a moment later: each one steers to the centre and the average heading, away from any too close, and away from a hunter
flockStep.notes: Reynolds' three rules, simplified for small flocks: cohesion and alignment steer toward the whole flock's centre and average velocity, not each one's neighbours'. The flock is moved one after another, each seeing those already moved this moment. Fleeing a hunter is Reynolds' flee steering behaviour (1999); the band, the weave and keeping the centre in a stretch of the view are this almanac's own.
tests: the flock holds together: after a minute every bird is within 40 of the centre
birds keep their distance: after a minute no two are closer than a sixth of the separation distance
every speed stays between the least and the most, times each one's own
a flock flees a hunter: in a second its centre moves away from it
a band brings a flock back to its heights
it changes nothing it is given, and gives every one its heading and its tilt

gridWalk.does: a walker on a grid a moment later: toward the middle of its next tile, and on arriving, a random allowed neighbour next, sometimes after a pause
gridWalk.notes: A random walk on a grid with a rule for which steps are allowed (onto land, not up a cliff, say) and pauses on arrival, so walkers look as if they stop to look about.
tests: a walker only ever steps to a neighbouring tile it may step to
it walks at its speed and arrives within a twentieth of a tile of the middle it set out for
on arriving it pauses about as often as asked: a quarter of 4,000 arrivals, give or take 2%

particleField.does: many small things strewn at random over a field, each with a depth, a phase and a number of its own
tests: every particle starts inside the field, at a depth from 0.4 to 1, with a phase and a number of its own
the same seed gives the same field

branchingTree.does: a branching thing (a tree, a coral, a crystal antler): a trunk that forks, each branch shorter and thinner, to the tips
branchingTree.notes: A recursive branching model, the kind The Algorithmic Beauty of Plants describes in its chapter on modeling trees; no L-system grammar is used. Each fork is fanned evenly across the spread and turned a little at random, and each branch's length varies by up to 15% shorter or 10% longer, so no two trees from different seeds are alike.
tests: a tree of L levels and F forks has (F^L - 1) / (F - 1) branches and F^(L - 1) tips
every branch grows from the end of the one before it, and the tips are the ends of the last level
each level is thinner by the decay, and shorter by the decay give or take 15%
the same seed gives the same tree, and another seed another

stampCache.does: a cache of things drawn once and stamped many times, forgetting the oldest past its limit
stampCache.notes: Forgetting the oldest first (not the least recently used) keeps it a few lines long; a world that holds steady fills it once and then only reads.
tests: it makes each key once, and past its limit forgets the oldest first

grain.does: grain over a whole picture (paper, film): a fixed texture of fine noise laid over everything by a blend mode
grain.notes: The texture is a 128-pixel tile, made once per picture size. Its greys come from multiplicative hashing of each pixel's number, by 2654435761, a prime close to 2 to the 32nd divided by the golden ratio.
tests: with no amount it draws nothing; with some, a flat grey picture gets a fine texture that keeps its average
its texture repeats every 128 pixels

vignette.does: the picture darkened toward its edges and corners, its middle left clear
tests: it darkens the corners and leaves the middle as it was; with no amount it draws nothing

mirrorBelow.does: a mirror of what is already drawn above a line, laid below it, fading and rippling (a wet street, a still lake)
mirrorBelow.notes: The mirror is copied from the picture already drawn (a screen-space reflection), strip by strip, so it must be drawn after what it reflects. Each strip is shifted by a ripple that grows toward the bottom, and is fainter the further down it is.
tests: below the line it shows what is above, upside down, and above the line nothing changes

drawList.does: draws a display list: a drawing given as data (shapes with their fills and strokes, and groups that move, blend or shade them)
drawList.notes: The shapes use the canvas's own path commands, so a drawing moves into data one call at a time, and the pixels stay the same. Only what an item says is set; everything it leaves out stays as the canvas has it, as hand-written drawing does.
tests: it draws exactly what the same canvas calls draw, pixel for pixel, for every kind of shape, paint and group
a group's moves, blending and shadow end with it, and what an item leaves out stays as the canvas has it
empty items are skipped, and an unknown path command is refused with a message naming the commands
a group's clip limits what is drawn in it to the inside of its path

latticeHash.does: one well-mixed 32-bit number for a point of a grid and a seed: the whole number latticeRandom divides into [0, 1)
tests: it is latticeRandom's number before the division
the same point and seed give the same number; neighbouring points give unrelated ones

the same seed gives the same stream

angleDiff.does: the signed turn from one angle to another the short way round, between -pi and pi, however many times round either has gone

a turn just past half a circle is given the other way round

noiseTile.does: a square of value noise that tiles: its right edge meets its left and its bottom its top, so it can be scrolled for ever
tests: its edges meet: the step across the seam is no bigger than a step inside it
at the grid's points it is the lattice's own values, and between them it stays within them

packRgb.does: a colour as one 32-bit number the way an ImageData keeps a pixel when its bytes are read as a Uint32Array: 0xAABBGGRR, opaque
tests: written into a Uint32Array over an ImageData's bytes, it gives those bytes red, green, blue and an opaque alpha
parts with a fraction or outside 0..255 are cut to their low byte, as the bytes would be

mixPacked.does: two packed colours mixed, red, green and blue each a share of the way from one to the other

packedHsl.does: a packed colour from hue (degrees), saturation and lightness

packedToHsl.does: a packed colour's hue (degrees), saturation and lightness

bayerThreshold.does: the ordered-dithering threshold at a pixel: the 4 x 4 Bayer matrix repeated across the picture, as a number in 0..1
tests: its sixteen thresholds are the sixteen steps (n + 0.5) / 16, each once in every 4 x 4 square
a share t set against it lights about t of the pixels in any 4 x 4 square, spread out rather than clumped

heightWater.does: what a height of the land makes it by the rule lower is water, higher is ground: water as deep as it is low, a shore just above

ellipseRows.does: the rows a filled ellipse covers, each a run of whole pixels: the half-width at each row from the ellipse's equation, rounded inward

shadeEllipse.does: a shadow: the pixels under an ellipse multiplied darker, a little bluer than redder, the edge a pixel edge

tests: each of red, green and blue is multiplied and held at 255, cut to a whole number, and alpha is opaque

outlineSprite.does: a sprite's pixels with a line round them: every empty pixel touching a drawn one on a side, at the picture's edge too
tests: empty pixels touching a drawn one on a side become the line, at the picture edge too, and the input is unchanged

spriteFromRows.does: a sprite written as rows of letters, one letter a pixel, read through a palette, with room for a line round it

resampleList.does: a list of numbers stretched or squeezed to another length, each new value read in a straight line between the two it falls between

twoBoneLimb3d.does: a two-bone limb in three dimensions: where the knee goes for a foot (pulled in to its reach), bent toward a pole and never below the ground
