the knee bends toward the pole it is given, and never below the ground

chamferDistance.does: for every cell of a grid not marked zero, how far it is from the nearest that is, a step across costing 3 and a step diagonally 4, in two passes
tests: along a straight run the distance grows by 3 a cell, and along a diagonal by 4
cells marked zero stay 0, and every other cell is no further than its neighbour plus a step

gridAStar.does: a shortest way over a grid of open and blocked cells, eight ways, never cutting a corner past a blocked cell, with a budget of cells to look at
tests: on an open grid it walks straight and then diagonal, as short as the octile distance
it goes round a wall, never through it or past its corner, and gives up past its budget

segmentClear.does: whether a straight line between two points crosses anything: points along it a step apart, each asked whether it is open
tests: a line across open ground is clear and one through a blocked cell is not

straightenPath.does: a way of grid points made straight where it can be: a point kept only where the line from the last one kept to the next would cross something
tests: on open ground the way is one straight step to its end; round a corner it keeps the corner

floodFill.does: everything reachable from a start by steps, each node visited once by its id
tests: it finds every cell of an open region and none beyond a wall

untilSettled.does: a set grown until it stops growing: a pass over the rules run again for as long as the last one added anything
tests: what can be got through a chain of needs is all found, and what needs something never got is not

obliqueShear.does: the matrix of an oblique view looking straight down: vertical edges stay vertical and level lines level while depth runs up and across
tests: raising a point moves it straight up the screen, and moving it back moves it up and across by m

obliqueToScreen.does: where a point of the ground shows in that oblique view, from the camera's place: across, its offset plus m times its depth; down, its depth less its height
tests: a point raised by h shows h higher, and one moved back shows higher and to the side

terraceLevel.does: how many terraces stand at a point: its height above the water's cut counted in whole steps, from none to the most
tests: it counts whole steps above the water and never goes below none or above the most

footStep.does: where a foot is at a moment of its step: lifted and swinging forward for half of it, planted for the other half
footStep.purpose: a walk cycle from two numbers (how far the foot reaches, how high it lifts) that any leg can follow, so a creature's walk is a phase and not a set of drawn frames

inspiration.text: the gait cycle: every foot alternates a stance phase, planted, and a swing phase, lifted
a walking foot rises and falls once while it swings, and is highest about half way

footStep.inWords: The step is a circle turning once. Its forward part, the sine, carries the foot from behind its rest point to in front of it and back. Its upward part, the cosine, lifts the foot only while it is positive, which is the half of the circle where the foot swings forward; for the other half the foot is held on the ground.
tests: the foot is on the ground for half the step and in the air for the other half
it swings forward while lifted and moves back while planted, never further than the stride
it is highest, at the lift, in the middle of its swing

strideRate.does: how far a step's phase turns for each unit the body walks, so a planted foot ends its stance where it landed
strideRate.purpose: the walk's speed and the legs' speed agree, whatever the leg length, so a long-legged heron and a short-legged crab both walk without skating away from where they stepped

inspiration.text: a planted foot stays where it was put down while the body passes over it

strideRate.inWords: While a foot is planted, its step turns half way round and footStep moves it back by twice its stride. If the body moves forward by the same twice-the-stride in that time, the two cancel and the foot ends where it was put down. So the phase turns half a circle for every two strides walked. In between, the foot does slide a little, forward and then back, by at most about a fifth of its stride: footStep moves a planted foot along a sine, while the body moves at a steady pace. A planted half that moved in a straight line would remove the slide; that would be a new technique, and it would change every picture made with this one.
tests: walking at the rate, a planted foot ends its stance where it was put down
in between, it slides by at most 0.211 of its stride

genomeFrom.does: an individual's genes, drawn from the ranges of its kind: no two alike, each clearly its kind
genomeFrom.purpose: endless distinct individuals from a few lines of data: a sprite sheet gives one cat; this gives every cat, the same one again from the same seed

inspiration.text: breeds and individuals of one species differ in proportion and markings, not in body plan

genomeFrom.inWords: A kind is a table: for each gene, a range of numbers, a list of choices, a chance, or a fixed value. An individual is one draw from each, in the table's order, from a generator seeded by the individual's name or number. The body plan stays the kind's; only the values inside it vary.
tests: the same seed always gives the same individual
every number is inside its range, every choice is from its list, every chance is true or false, and fixed values are kept
different seeds give different individuals
it draws once for each gene that is not fixed, in order, so the caller can go on drawing from the same generator

crossGenomes.does: a child's genes from two parents of one kind: each number mixed between theirs, each choice one parent's, and now and then a gene that mutates, never leaving its kind
crossGenomes.purpose: creatures that breed: a child that is visibly its parents' (their proportions mixed, a marking from one of them) and yet its own, so a herd can grow from its own kind instead of from fresh draws

inspiration.text: recombination in evolutionary algorithms: discrete recombination takes each gene from one parent, intermediate recombination mixes a real-valued gene between the two
mutation with regard to restrictions: a gene moved by a small random step and held inside its allowed range
a foal has its own face, but its legs and its coat plainly come from its mother and its sire

crossGenomes.inWords: Both parents are individuals of one kind, so each gene has a range, a list, a chance or a fixed value. A number becomes a point picked at random on the line between the parents' two values. A choice or a chance is a coin toss between the two. Then each gene, with a small probability, mutates: a number moves by up to that same share of its range, a choice is drawn afresh from its list, a chance flips; and a number is held inside its range, so the child is always its kind. A gene neither parent has is drawn from the kind as genomeFrom draws it.
tests: the same parents and the same seed always give the same child
with no mutation, every number lies between its parents and every other gene is one of theirs
with mutation, every gene stays inside its kind: numbers in their range, choices from their list
two parents alike give a child just like them when nothing mutates
children of one pair differ from one another, each a new mix of the two

indexRandom.does: a number in [0, 1) for an index and a seed, the same every time
indexRandom.purpose: things placed by their number (the 7th star, the 12th building, the 3rd cloud) need their own random numbers without a generator to carry from frame to frame

inspiration.text: an integer hash spreads neighbouring numbers far apart

indexRandom.inWords: The index is multiplied by a large odd number, mixed with the hashed seed, hashed again, and divided by 2 to the 32nd power. The same index and seed always land on the same number; the next index lands somewhere unrelated.
tests: the same index and seed give the same number, in [0, 1)
neighbouring indices give unrelated numbers: over 10,000 of them each tenth of [0, 1) gets 10%, give or take 0.6%

hueToward.does: a hue moved part of the way toward another, the short way round; far hues only lean
hueToward.purpose: colour grades that pull every colour toward one hue without turning any of them into a third colour

inspiration.text: pulled all the way toward blue, an orange passes through magenta on the way; a grade should make it a cooler orange, not a purple

hueToward.inWords: Hues are angles on the colour wheel. The move goes the short way round. When the target is more than 100 degrees away, only a quarter of the move is made, so the colour leans toward the target and keeps its own family.
tests: it moves a hue the short way round the wheel, by the share asked
a hue more than 100 degrees away moves only a quarter as far

gradeColour.does: a colour graded as a film is graded: a range of hues moved, then the whole picture shifted, saturated, lit, contrasted and warmed
gradeColour.purpose: one picture shown in many moods (golden hour, moonlit, faded print) by changing a handful of numbers, not the picture

inspiration.text: colour grading in film, where a whole picture is moved toward a mood after it is shot
seasons change the greens of a landscape and leave its stone and sky alone

gradeColour.inWords: The colour is read as hue, saturation and lightness. If it is in the given range of hues (and coloured enough to count), it moves toward that range's own hue first: that is how greens turn gold in autumn. Then every colour leans toward the grade's hue, has its saturation scaled, its lightness raised, its contrast stretched round the middle, and, last, is warmed by adding red and taking away blue.
tests: an empty grade gives the colour back
warmth adds red and takes away blue
a hue range moves only the colours whose hue is in it
contrast stretches lightness away from the middle

dayCycle.does: the day at a moment: the sky's colours, how much light there is, where the sun and the moon are
dayCycle.purpose: a whole day's light from four pairs of colours, so a world can be shown at any moment without anyone painting its dusk

inspiration.text: key frames: a few moments set by hand, the ones between filled in
dawn and dusk are brief and night and day are long; the light comes before the sun is high

dayCycle.inWords: The day is a ring: 0 is midnight, 0.25 dawn, 0.5 noon, 0.75 dusk. Eight keys hold the night's colours until 0.21, pass through dawn's at 0.27 into day's by 0.36, hold day until 0.64, and pass through dusk's at 0.73 back into night by 0.79; between two keys the colours are blended in proportion. The light is a sine wave over the day, lifted and stretched so it is full from about 7:40 to 16:20 and none from about 18:50 to 5:10. The sun crosses the sky in the day's half of the ring, and the moon in the other half.
tests: at noon it is full light and the sky is the day's; at midnight full dark and the night's
the colours and the light change smoothly all day: no jump anywhere
the light is full from about 7:40 to 16:20 and none from about 18:50 to 5:10
the sun is highest at noon and below the horizon at midnight, and the moon the other way round

twinkle.does: how bright a twinkling star is at a moment: a slow swell and fade at its own phase
twinkle.purpose: stars that twinkle with no generator and no stored state: brightness is a function of the time and the star's own phase

inspiration.text: stars twinkle because the air between them and the eye keeps moving

twinkle.inWords: Each star has a phase of its own. Its brightness is a sine wave of the time, shifted by that phase, swinging between full and 1 - 2 depth. Neighbouring stars are at different points of the wave, so the sky shimmers rather than pulses.
tests: it swings between 1 and 1 - 2 depth, round 1 - depth

hillLine.does: the outline of a line of hills, side-on: noise at four scales, sharpened into peaks or stepped into terraces if asked
hillLine.purpose: endless hills from a handful of numbers (how many, how high, how sharp, how rough, stepped or not) that scroll past without repeating

inspiration.text: fractal noise: detail at every scale, as in real ridgelines
mesas and rice terraces: land that rises in flat steps

hillLine.inWords: Noise along the line is read at four scales, each about twice as fine as the last and fainter by the roughness. Sharpness folds each scale at its middle, toward a ridge. The sum hugs the middle (an average always does), so it is stretched 2.6 times about the middle to reach the full range, and, for terraces, rounded to so many steps. The result places the land between its base and its height.
tests: the land stays between the base and the base less the height
flat hills are a level line, and terraced hills have only so many heights
the line is unbroken: a hundredth of a pixel along, it moves by less than a twentieth

islandHeight.does: an island's height at a tile: fractal noise lowered toward the map's edge and lifted toward its middle
islandHeight.purpose: an island that always rises out of the sea in the middle of its map and sinks into it all round, never touching the edge, from a seed

inspiration.text: shaping noise into an island by lowering it with distance from the middle
a heightmap: land as a grid of heights

islandHeight.inWords: Fractal noise gives the land its shape. It is multiplied down by the distance from the middle (as that distance to the power 2.2, so the coast falls away quickly near the edge) and lifted by a quarter in the middle. A long island measures its distance as if the map were squeezed, so it stretches along one axis.
tests: it stays within 0 to 1, and the same tile and seed give the same height
the edge of the map is sea and the middle is land: over 50 seeds the border averages under a tenth, the centre over a half

scatterAlong.does: things scattered along a line: a slot every so often, kept by chance, nudged within it, with a variant and a size
scatterAlong.purpose: trees on a hillside or houses along a street that look placed by nature, never in rows and never in clumps, and are the same things every time they scroll back into view

inspiration.text: jittered sampling: one sample in each cell of a grid, nudged at random within it, spreads points evenly without lining them up

scatterAlong.inWords: The line is cut into slots of equal width, numbered from its start. Each slot draws its own numbers from its index and the seed: whether it is kept, how far it is nudged (up to 40% of a slot either way), which variant it is and how big. Because the numbers come from the slot's index and not from a running generator, any stretch of the line can be asked for, in any order, and gives the same things.
tests: about the share asked for of the slots are kept: 70% of 10,000, give or take 1.5%
each thing stays in its own slot, nudged by at most 40% of a slot either way
the same slot is the same thing whatever stretch it is asked for in
sizes stay in their range and variants are whole numbers below the count

windowLit.does: whether a window is lit: a fixed share of windows, a pattern that changes every 25 seconds, each building on its own schedule
windowLit.purpose: a city at night that is never still and never flickers: windows go dark and light a building at a time

inspiration.text: lit windows in a city at night: a share of them, changing over the evening, one building here and one there

windowLit.inWords: Each window draws a number from its building, row, column, the seed and the current period. A period is 25 seconds long, and each building's periods begin at their own offset, so the buildings do not all change at once. A window is lit when its number is under the share.
tests: about the share asked for of the windows are lit: 40% of 20,000, give or take 1.5%
a building's pattern holds for 25 seconds and then changes, and buildings change at different moments

blink.does: whether a blinking light is on: on while a wave at its own rate and phase is above a threshold
blink.purpose: beacons, failing neon and signal lamps, each at its own rhythm, with no state to keep

inspiration.text: the red beacon on a tower, and a neon sign that fails in brief dips

blink.inWords: A sine wave at the light's rate, shifted by its phase, is compared with the threshold. Above it the light is on, so the threshold sets the share of each cycle it shines: 1/2 - asin(threshold)/π.
tests: it is on for 1/2 - asin(threshold)/π of each cycle

faceShade.does: how much darker a wall is than the ground on top of it, by which way it faces the light
faceShade.purpose: blocks of land that read as solid from every side as the island turns, each wall shaded by how it faces a light fixed to the island

inspiration.text: Lambert's law: a surface is lit in proportion to how squarely it faces the light

faceShade.inWords: How squarely the wall faces the light is the dot product of the two directions: 1 facing it, 0 side-on, -1 facing away. The shade runs from -0.18 at 1 to -0.40 at -1 in a straight line. Unlike Lambert's law, a wall facing away is never black: the land keeps its colour on every side.
tests: a wall facing the light gets -0.18, one facing away -0.40, and one side-on to it half way between

pulseRise.does: something that rises in pulses (a jelly, a lantern, a spirit) a moment later: pushed up by each pulse, coasting between, swaying
pulseRise.purpose: jellies and lanterns that move as if alive, from a phase and the time, with nothing to remember between moments

inspiration.text: a jellyfish rises by squeezing its bell, then coasts and drifts until the next squeeze

pulseRise.inWords: The pulse is a wave at its own rate. Only its rising half pushes, by as much as the wave is high, so each pulse is a shove followed by a coast. A slow wave of the time, shifted by the thing's own number, sways it sideways.
tests: it rises in pulses and never sinks, and its sway stays within amount / rate either side (a thousandth over, for stepping)

fall.does: falling, a moment later (rain, snow, petals, leaves): down at its speed, blown by the wind, fluttering if asked
fall.purpose: every falling thing from one law and a few numbers: rain is fast and straight, snow slow and swaying, petals flutter and bob

inspiration.text: rain falls fast and straight; snow and petals fall slowly, swaying from side to side and bobbing; near ones cross the view faster than far ones

fall.inWords: Each moment the particle's phase turns at its own pace. It moves down at its speed and sideways with the wind, plus a sway (a sine of its phase) and a bob (a cosine of it), less the camera's drift. Both moves are scaled by its depth, so near particles fall and blow faster than far ones, which is what makes a field of them look deep.
tests: with no wind, sway or camera it falls straight down at its speed times its depth
wind blows it sideways and the camera carries it back, the near more than the far
its phase turns at its own pace, 1 + s a second

rise.does: rising, a moment later (bubbles, embers): up at its speed, each a little faster or slower, wobbling sideways
rise.purpose: bubbles and embers that rise as a crowd of individuals, not in step

inspiration.text: bubbles in water and sparks over a fire rise at different speeds and wobble as they go

rise.inWords: The particle rises at the slowest speed plus its own share of the spread (its number times the spread), so no two rise in step. It wobbles sideways by a sine of its phase, and drifts with the wind.
tests: it rises at its speed plus its share of the spread, and wobbles no further than amount / rate either side (a thousandth over, for stepping)

hover.does: hanging in the air, a moment later (dust, plankton, fireflies): wandering in small loops round where it is
hover.purpose: motes that hang in light or water, alive but going nowhere

inspiration.text: dust in a sunbeam and plankton in water drift in small loops and stay roughly where they are

hover.inWords: A sine of the phase moves it along x and a cosine at another rate along y, so it traces slow loops round its place. The camera's drift carries it back as the view moves on, by its depth if asked.
tests: with no camera it hangs where it is: over a minute it stays within its wander's reach
the camera carries it back, by its depth if asked

wrapAround.does: a particle that has left the field comes back on the far side, so the field never thins out
wrapAround.purpose: a field of particles that stays full however long the wind blows or the camera moves

inspiration.text: wraparound in video games: what leaves one edge of the screen enters at the opposite edge

wrapAround.inWords: A particle more than the margin past one edge is moved across the whole field plus both margins, so it reappears just past the margin of the opposite edge, off the screen, and drifts in.
tests: a particle past the margin on one side comes back past the margin on the other, and one inside is left alone

swayingChain.does: a chain swaying from a fixed foot (kelp, a vine, a reed, a banner): a wave runs up it, so the foot is still and the tip swings most
swayingChain.purpose: kelp in a current and reeds in the wind from a handful of numbers, alive without any physics to simulate

inspiration.text: kelp and tall grass: rooted still at the foot, swinging more the higher up, the swing running up the stem like a wave
forward kinematics: a chain of links placed one after another, each by its own angle

swayingChain.inWords: The chain is built link by link from its foot. Each link's angle is a sine wave of the time, a step further along the wave for each link up, scaled by how far up the link is, so the foot barely moves and the tip swings by the whole sway. Each link goes its own length in its own direction from the end of the last.
tests: it has as many links as segments, all the same length, starting at its foot
with no sway and no lean it stands straight up
each link leans at most sway times its share of the way up, so the foot is steady and the tip swings most

setCanvasMaker.does: says how canvases are made: in a browser by itself, in Node by the function it is given
setCanvasMaker.purpose: the same drawing code in a web page and in a test or a tool run from the command line

inspiration.text: OffscreenCanvas, the web standard for a canvas off the page, and @napi-rs/canvas (MIT), which draws the same 2D canvas in Node

setCanvasMaker.inWords: A browser makes an OffscreenCanvas if it can, or a canvas element. Node has neither, so a program running there says once, at the start, which function makes a canvas, and everything that needs one asks makeCanvas.
tests: after it, makeCanvas makes canvases the way it was told

makeCanvas.does: a new canvas, made the way setCanvasMaker said
makeCanvas.purpose: drawing helpers (grain, glows, stamps) that need a canvas of their own, without knowing where they run

inspiration.text: OffscreenCanvas in browsers; @napi-rs/canvas (MIT) in Node

makeCanvas.inWords: It calls the maker it was told about with the width and height asked for.
tests: it gives a canvas of the size asked, to draw on

partPath.does: the outline of a simple shape (blob, box, spike, tri, gem, dome, stem, disc, ring), standing on a point
partPath.purpose: a small vocabulary of shapes from which most things in a landscape can be built: rocks, bushes, houses, posts, crystals, lamps

inspiration.text: seen from far enough away, most things standing in a landscape are a few simple shapes

partPath.inWords: Each shape is a few lines or an ellipse, set on its base point, as wide and as tall as asked. A lean tilts its top (as a share of its height); a ring is an ellipse with a smaller one cut out of it.
tests: every shape stands on its point, as wide and as tall as asked, to within a pixel and a half
a ring has a hole, and an unknown shape is a box

fillInArt.does: fills a shape in an art style: flat, gradient, facet (split hard, like cut stone) or glowing, with a paper shadow and an outline if asked
fillInArt.purpose: one world drawn in many looks by changing a word: flat paper, soft gradients, low-poly facets, neon glow

inspiration.text: cel shading: flat colour with hard-edged light and shade, as in cartoons
paper cut-outs, with their soft shadows; low-poly art, with its hard facets; neon at night

fillInArt.inWords: A gradient runs from the upper left, lighter, through the colour, to the lower right, darker. A facet is the same gradient with its middle stop doubled, so the colour steps instead of blending. A glow adds a halo by a canvas shadow in a lighter tint. A paper shadow is a soft dark shadow just below the shape.
tests: flat art fills in exactly the colour; gradient art is lighter at the top left than at the bottom right
facet art steps from light to dark across the middle instead of blending, and a line is drawn round when asked

drawRecipe.does: draws a recipe: a few simple shapes in their colours and the art's style, some repeated and scattered, each repeat a little different
drawRecipe.purpose: a bush, a house, a coral or a lamp written as a few lines of data, and drawn a little differently every time it appears

inspiration.text: no two bushes are the same, but every bush is the same few shapes

drawRecipe.inWords: Each part of the recipe is drawn its count of times. Each time its size varies by its jitter, its place by its spread, and its lean by a little (and, when there are several, to one side or the other). The generator decides all of it, so the same seed draws the same thing.
tests: the same seed draws the same picture, pixel for pixel, and another seed another
a part repeated is drawn that many times, spread about its place

glowSprite.does: a small soft glow in a colour, drawn once and kept, to stamp wherever something glows
glowSprite.purpose: hundreds of fireflies, lamps and lit windows glowing at once, cheaply: a blur on each would be far slower

inspiration.text: sprites: an image drawn once and stamped many times

glowSprite.inWords: A 16-pixel canvas is filled with a round gradient: the colour at the middle, half as strong a third of the way out, nothing at the edge. It is kept, by colour, and stamped scaled to any size.
tests: it is strongest in the middle and gone at the edges, and the same colour gives the very same canvas

glowingDisc.does: a glowing disc (the sun, the moon, a lamp): a soft halo four and a half times its size, and the disc
glowingDisc.purpose: a sun and a moon that glow in any sky, from a colour, a size and a strength

inspiration.text: the sun and the moon seen through air: a bright disc in a soft glow that fades into the sky

glowingDisc.inWords: A round gradient from half the radius out to four and a half radii fades the colour from part strength to nothing; the disc is drawn solid over it.
tests: the disc is solid in its colour, and its halo fades to nothing by four and a half radii

lightRays.does: light rays from above (sunbeams through cloud, light through water): slanting shafts fading downward, added onto the picture
lightRays.purpose: sunbeams and underwater light that drift slowly, from a count, a colour and a seed

inspiration.text: crepuscular rays: shafts of light through gaps, made visible by the air or water

lightRays.inWords: Each shaft is a slanted four-sided shape, placed and sized by its number and the seed, swaying a little with the time. It is filled with its colour fading to nothing downward, and added to the picture (the 'lighter' blend), so where shafts cross they brighten, and they never darken anything.
tests: rays only ever lighten the picture, and fade from the top downward

fogBands.does: fog lying in a band of the picture: three soft layers, thickest in their middles
fogBands.purpose: mist in a valley or haze over water, in front of some layers and behind others

inspiration.text: fog lies in layers in low ground, densest in the middle of its layer and thinning above and below

fogBands.inWords: Three horizontal bands spread through the fog's band, each a gradient from clear to the fog's colour and back, rising and falling a little with the time.
tests: fog is thickest in its band and leaves the picture well above it clear

puffCloud.does: a cloud of six round puffs along a gentle arch, with a soft shadow below and to the right
puffCloud.purpose: storybook clouds from a place, a size and a colour, each a little different by its number

inspiration.text: cartoon and storybook clouds, drawn as a row of round puffs with a shadow

puffCloud.inWords: Six circles sit along an arch, the middle ones higher, each a little larger or smaller by a sine of its place and the cloud's number. The same six are drawn first in the shadow colour, down and to the right, then in the cloud's own.
tests: its shadow lies below it and to the right, and it is about 44 pixels across at size 1

inkedLine.does: a line of land inked, the way comics ink it: a dark line, and light hatching under it that travels with the land
inkedLine.purpose: an ink-and-wash or comic look for any landscape, from the line of its land

inspiration.text: hatching: shading drawn as close parallel lines, as in ink drawings and comics

inkedLine.inWords: The line is stroked in a near-black of the land's colour, darker and thicker the nearer the land. Under it, inside the land, slanting strokes start a little below the line, spaced evenly and shifted by how far the land has scrolled, so the hatching moves with the land and does not slide over it.
tests: the ink follows the line, and the hatching lies only below it

tones.does: a colour's tones for soft shading: a dark leaning blue-violet, the colour, a light leaning warm cream, and a deep line colour
tones.purpose: shading that looks painted rather than computed, from one colour

inspiration.text: painters and pixel artists shade with cooler shadows and warmer lights, not just darker and lighter

tones.inWords: The dark is the colour darkened by a third and moved a seventh of the way toward a deep blue-violet; the light is the colour lightened by a fifth and moved a seventh of the way toward a warm cream; the line is the colour darkened by two thirds and moved toward a near-black purple.
tests: dark is darker and bluer than the colour, light is lighter and warmer, and line is the darkest

drawParts.does: a figure of simple parts drawn as a hand-drawn sprite is: a ground shadow, one outline round everything, each part soft-shaded in three tones
drawParts.purpose: creatures and characters made of a few ellipses and limbs that look drawn, at any size and facing either way

inspiration.text: cel shading and hand-drawn sprites: an outline round the whole figure, flat tones with a lit side and a highlight

drawParts.inWords: First a soft shadow on the ground. Then every part is drawn grown by the outline's width in the line colour, which leaves one outline round the whole figure. Then the parts, far to near: each in its dark tone; the same shape moved up and to the left, clipped to the part, in its base tone, which leaves a shadow on the lower right; and on large parts a smaller shape further up and left in the light tone. Eyes are dark with a catchlight. Facing left is the same drawing mirrored.
tests: facing left is facing right mirrored, pixel for pixel
one outline goes round the figure in the line colour, and the figure is shaded lighter toward the upper left
flat art fills each part in its base tone
nearer parts cover farther ones: drawn in the order of z, whatever order they are given in

seedOf.does: the seed a value stands for: a number is itself, words are hashed to a number from 1 to 99,999
seedOf.purpose: seeds people can share by saying them: a world given as amber-vale-7 grows the same for everyone who types it, in any case

inspiration.text: two words and a small number are easier to say, remember and share than a long number
a string hash turns any text into a number, the same every time

seedOf.inWords: Spaces at the ends are dropped. A whole number is taken as it is (and 0 becomes 1). Anything else is lowered to one case, hashed (hashString), and brought into 1 to 99,999 by a remainder, so that the seed is short enough to show and to type.
tests: a whole number is itself (at least 1), and nothing is 1
words give a number from 1 to 99,999, the same whatever their case or the spaces at their ends

seedWords.does: a new seed as words: a word from each of two lists and a number from 1 to 99, joined by hyphens
seedWords.purpose: new seeds that are already easy to share, from word lists that fit the program (an adjective, a place)

inspiration.text: two words and a small number are easier to say, remember and share than a long number

seedWords.inWords: It picks a word from the first list and one from the second, each as likely, and a number from 1 to 99, and joins them with hyphens. seedOf turns the result into the number a program grows its world from.
tests: it gives a word from each list and a number from 1 to 99, joined by hyphens
the same random numbers give the same words

tracePart.does: a figure part's outline added to the path being built, grown or shrunk if asked
tracePart.purpose: drawing over a part clipped to it (a belly, spots, stripes, a shell's seam) with the very outline drawParts fills

inspiration.text: markings are drawn inside a body's outline, never over its edge

tracePart.inWords: An ellipse, a tapered limb or a polygon is traced as drawParts traces it; a body traces each of its ellipses, so filling or clipping takes them together. A grow enlarges every radius by that many pixels.
tests: a traced body is its ellipses together, and a traced part grown by a pixel covers the part and a ring round it

partOutline.does: a figure part's outline as path commands (data): an ellipse, a tapered limb, a polygon, or a body's ellipses together
partOutline.purpose: the very outline drawParts fills, as data a program can keep, pass on, or clip a display list to

inspiration.text: a path given as data, as display lists and vector formats give it

partOutline.inWords: Each kind of part becomes the canvas commands that trace it: an ellipse is one ellipse; a tapered limb is two arcs, one at each end, closed; a polygon is its corners joined and closed; a body is each of its ellipses. A grow enlarges every radius by that many pixels. tracePart and drawParts trace these same commands.
tests: traced, its commands give the very pixels tracePart gives, for every kind of part

hueShiftTone.does: a pixel artist's shade of a colour: darker turns toward blue-violet and richer, lighter toward warm yellow and paler
hueShiftTone.purpose: shading that looks lit: one colour's ramp of darker and lighter steps for a sprite, as a pixel artist makes it by hand

inspiration.text: pixel artists' ramps that shift hue as they shift lightness: cooler and richer into shadow, warmer and paler into light
綴 Tsuzuri's 言の葉, whose creatures, plants and lands are shaded with it

hueShiftTone.inWords: The colour is taken to hue, saturation and lightness. Going darker, its hue is turned part of the way toward blue-violet (250 degrees), its saturation raised and its lightness multiplied down by a fifth a step; going lighter, its hue is turned toward warm yellow (52 degrees), its saturation lowered and its lightness raised toward white by about a quarter of what is left a step. Each step turns the hue by up to 7.5% of the way, never more than a third, and pale colours (lightness over 0.72) turn and change saturation by less than half as much, so a light colour is not tinted out of itself.
tests: darker steps are darker and turn toward blue-violet; lighter steps are lighter and turn toward warm yellow
zero steps gives the colour back, to within a byte's rounding, except that it is never quite black or quite white

ditheredBorder.does: whether a pixel near the border of two regions belongs to the other: its share there set against the Bayer pattern, with a little noise
ditheredBorder.purpose: a border between two lands, two textures or two seasons that reads as a band of mixed pixels thinning out, not a line, and holds still as the picture moves

inspiration.text: ordered dithering: a share shown by the fraction of pixels lit, in the Bayer pattern

ditheredBorder.inWords: Each pixel has the share f of the other region at it (none on the far side of the band, rising toward the border) and a random number of its own. It belongs to the other region when f is above zero and above half the Bayer threshold there, nudged by a quarter of its random number's distance from the middle: the pattern spreads the other region's pixels evenly, and the noise keeps the pattern from showing as a screen.
tests: with no share of the other, never; with a whole share, always
the share of pixels that go to the other rises with f across a band

levelCut.does: the height that a given share of a land made from fractal noise lies below, so water can be set by how much of the land it covers
levelCut.purpose: lands whose water is asked for as a share (a sea that covers seventy per cent, a pond a fifth) rather than as a height that means nothing on its own

inspiration.text: terrain from noise: thresholds on the noise's height decide water, shore and ground
the probit, the normal distribution's quantile: fractal noise is about bell-shaped round its middle

levelCut.inWords: Fractal noise is about bell-shaped round 0.5, with a spread of about 0.105. The share asked for is looked up in a table of the normal distribution's quantiles at every twentieth (the probits of 0.05, 0.10 and so on, cut off at three standard deviations at the ends), between two entries in a straight line, and scaled by the spread round 0.5.
tests: about the share of fractal noise it is asked for lies below it
a bigger share gives a higher cut, and a half gives the middle, 0.5

wanderingHeading.does: the next heading of a path that wanders by itself: toward a heading that drifts with noise along its length, turning no more than a set amount a step
wanderingHeading.purpose: a trail across a land that curves like a path walked, never zigzags, and is the same from the same seed

inspiration.text: a random walk, with its turns made smooth by noise along the path instead of drawn fresh at each step

wanderingHeading.inWords: The heading the path wants is its overall bias plus noise along its length: fractal noise that drifts over about five hundred steps (up to about a radian either way) and value noise over about a hundred (a little more). The path turns toward that heading by the short way round, but never by more than the set turn a step (0.06 radians), so its curves are gentle however the wanted heading jumps.
tests: it never turns by more than the set amount in a step
the same seed walks the same path, another seed another

waterTime.does: the water's clock at a moment: the whole-pixel offsets its swells, ripples and glints have drifted to, worked out once for every pixel
waterTime.purpose: water that moves without being stepped: every pixel of a frame read from the same few offsets, the same at the same moment every time

inspiration.text: tiles of value noise read at offsets that grow with time

waterTime.inWords: From the time in seconds: the swell's offsets across and down (6 and 2 pixels a second), two ripples' (15, and 10 across with 4 down), and the glints' beat (3 a second), each cut to a whole pixel; and the frame count at fifteen a second, which the foam flickers with.
tests: its offsets are whole numbers that grow with time, each at its own rate

waterPixel.does: one pixel of water seen from above: foam lapping a beach, deeper darker, swells and ripples, glints on the crests, sand in the shallows, weed on the bed
waterPixel.purpose: water in pixel art that lives: seen into, moving, catching light, lapping its shores, drawn a pixel at a time with no state

inspiration.text: tiles of value noise that wrap, read at moving offsets

waterPixel.inWords: Within a breathing width of a beach (or a pixel of a wall) it is foam. Otherwise its depth step is set by how far it is from the shore, then moved lighter or darker by a broad swell tile and by two fine ripple tiles averaged (their crests drawn out sideways), each read at the clock's offsets, and darker again where a bank shades it. On a crest a short dash may glint, on a beat of its own. Close to a beach the bed shows as sand; elsewhere a slow tile of weed patches shimmers through. Four tiles of wrapping noise, made once from fixed seeds, are all its texture.
tests: it gives only the palette's colours
by a beach it is foam at the edge and sand in the shallows; out in open water it is the water's own steps
deep water far from the shore is darker on the whole than water near it
the same pixel at the same moment is the same colour; as time goes on it changes

fillBetweenEdges.does: rows of a letter grid filled across between their outermost drawn letters, the ends in one letter and each half in its own
fillBetweenEdges.purpose: one piece of cloth over parts drawn apart: a robe over two legs, filled to whatever width the legs and their outline reach

inspiration.text: a scanline fill: a row filled between its edges

fillBetweenEdges.inWords: For each row from the first to the one before the last, the columns that hold any letter but '.' are found; if there are none the row is left. Every column from the leftmost of them to the rightmost is then written: the leftmost and the rightmost in the edge letter, the columns up to the middle (a half included) in the near letter, the rest in the far letter.
tests: each row is filled from its first drawn letter to its last, ends in the edge letter and halves in the near and far letters

leafCrown.does: a crown of leaves in a pixel buffer: round clumps scattered about a middle, each pixel shaded by its nearest clump and by the crown as a whole, in four steps
leafCrown.purpose: a tree that reads as leaves at a few dozen pixels across: clumps that each catch the light, inside a crown that is lit as one shape

inspiration.text: a Voronoi partition: each pixel belongs to the clump nearest it, measured in that clump's radii
cel shading: the light in a few flat steps rather than a smooth ramp

leafCrown.inWords: The crown has n clumps (given, or rx times ry over 7, at least 4). Each is set at a random angle and a distance of the square root of a random number times the spread (0.62 unless given) of the half-axes from the middle, with a radius of 0.34 to 0.52 of the smaller half-axis plus 0.8; one more sits at the middle with 0.6 of it. All are filled with a marker colour, and the marked pixels are the inside. Each inside pixel takes the clump nearest it in clump radii. Its light t is 0.55 times the whole crown's (0.55 of its leftness plus 0.85 of its height, in half-axes) plus 1.25 times the clump's own (1 less its distance from a point up and left of the clump's middle, in 1.05 radii, less 0.42), plus 0.1 on one pixel in five of a fixed pattern. Over 0.72 it is the brightest leaf colour, over 0.18 the light, over -0.42 the mid, else the dark. With a blossom colour, the inside pixels where (31x + 17y + seed) is a multiple of bloomEvery (9 unless given) and are not the dark take it.
tests: the same seed draws the same crown, lit more on its upper left than its lower right, in only the four leaf colours

barkTrunk.does: a tree's trunk in a pixel buffer: a column from top to foot, leaning at the top, a pixel wider near the foot, lit down its left side
barkTrunk.purpose: a trunk under a crown that stands on the ground and leans a little, drawn in whole pixels as a pixel artist would

inspiration.text: pixel art drawn a pixel at a time, lit from the upper left

barkTrunk.inWords: For each row from the top (rounded) to the foot, u is how far down the row is (0 at the top, 1 at the foot). The row's middle is x plus the lean times 1 - u, rounded, and its width is the width given, one more where u is over 0.8. The row's pixels run from the middle less half the width (rounded down); the first is the light bark where the row is wider than one pixel, the rest the dark. Pixels outside the buffer are left.
tests: it fills its column from top to foot, leaning only at the top, a pixel wider near the foot, its left column the light bark

followJoint.does: where a point of a chain goes when the point before it has moved: back toward where it was at its set distance, turned no more than a set angle from the way the chain runs
followJoint.purpose: a spine, a tail or a neck that follows its head and bends only as far as a body bends, from points alone

inspiration.text: procedural animation: a chain of points each kept a set distance behind the one before

followJoint.inWords: Take the angle from the point before to where this point was. Measure how far it turns from the way the chain runs there (pointing back), clamp that turn to the bend allowed, and put the point at its distance from the point before, along the clamped angle.
tests: the point lands at its set distance from the point before it
it never turns more than its bend from the way the chain runs

footSwing.does: where a foot is during its step: from where it lifted to where it lands, eased at both ends, raised in an arc highest half way
footSwing.purpose: steps that leave and land gently and lift off the ground, for feet planted by footReady

inspiration.text: the swing phase of a gait: the foot lifted and carried forward
smoothstep: an S-curve that starts and ends level

footSwing.inWords: With t the step's progress, e = 3t^2 - 2t^3. Across and down are read from lift-off to landing at e; the height is the lift times sin(pi t).
tests: the foot leaves where it lifted, lands where it lands, and is highest half way

footReady.does: whether a planted foot steps now: once the body has left it half a stride behind (or a little, standing nearly still), and only while the other group of feet is down unless it is left almost a stride behind
footReady.purpose: feet that stay planted until the body leaves them, and diagonal pairs that take turns, with no gait clock to keep

inspiration.text: the stance phase of a gait: a foot stays planted while the body passes over it
animals walking: a foot is lifted when the body has moved past it, and the diagonal pairs alternate

footReady.inWords: A foot is far when it is more than half a stride from where it would rest, or, if the body moves at under 1.5 and no foot is stepping, more than 1.2 of the body's scale away. A far foot steps if no foot of the other group is stepping, or if it is more than 0.95 of a stride away.
tests: a foot left half a stride behind steps, but waits while the other group is stepping unless left almost a stride

floatHeight.does: how high a part of a floating body rides: head held up, neck parts a little under, the middle low, the tail just under the surface, a bird high on it, with a slow swell along the body
floatHeight.purpose: animals that swim in the water rather than on it or under it, from their parts' radii alone

inspiration.text: buoyancy: a floating body sits partly under the surface
swimming animals: the head is held up, the back low, the tail trails just under; ducks sit high

floatHeight.inWords: The head rides at 0.8 of its radius above the surface (1.4 for a bird). A neck part rides at -0.1 of its radius (0.55 for a bird), a tail part at -0.95 (0.3), the rest at -0.72 (0.25). A swell of 0.3 times the body's scale (at most 1) runs down the body: sin(2.4 t - 0.55 i).
tests: afloat, the head rides above the water and the middle and the tail below it, a bird above it all along

depthUnderCut.does: how far a pixel of a round part is under a level surface, seen from above and in front: the surface cuts along the front of the part's ring, lowest in the middle of the cut
depthUnderCut.purpose: a body swimming toward or away from the eye in the water all along it, never cut by one straight line

inspiration.text: the chord a level plane cuts through a round part

depthUnderCut.inWords: Across the cut, u runs from -1 to 1. The surface's row there is the row under the part's middle plus half the cut's half width times sqrt(1 - u^2); the pixel's middle below that row is how far under it is.
tests: the surface lies lowest in the middle of the cut and rises to its ends

despeckle.does: a lone pixel whose four neighbours are mostly one other colour takes that colour, read from a copy so changes do not cascade
despeckle.purpose: clean blocks of colour in a small sprite built from overlapping shapes, without the in-between specks that read as blur

inspiration.text: filtering a picture by its neighbourhood to remove specks

despeckle.inWords: For each filled pixel with four filled neighbours none of which is its own colour: if two of the neighbours share a colour (checked left with right, up and down, then right with up and down, then up with down), it takes that colour.
tests: a lone speck among one colour takes that colour, and blocks are left as they are

staggeredScales.does: scales on a sprite: on every other row, every third pixel of two colours turns to its darker shade, rows staggered, anchored to the body
staggeredScales.purpose: a scaly skin that stays put on the body as it moves, in two of its colours

inspiration.text: hatching: texture from a regular pattern of marks

staggeredScales.inWords: On even rows (counted from the body's anchor), a pixel of either colour turns dark where (column + anchor + 2 when the row's half is odd + 300) is a multiple of 3.
tests: scales fall on every other row, one in three, staggered, and only on the two colours given

topEdgeShine.does: a shine along the top edge of the left part of a sprite: a column's top pixel, if it has a pixel under it, turns a lighter shade
topEdgeShine.purpose: shells and hard backs that catch light from the upper left

inspiration.text: cel shading: light shown as a band of lighter colour
a lighter shade turned warmer, as pixel artists ramp a colour

topEdgeShine.inWords: Find the sprite's left and right columns. For each column from one past the left to the left plus 45 per cent of the width (at least 2), the top pixel lightens by 1.6 steps of hueShiftTone if the pixel under it is filled and the one over it is not.
tests: only top-edge pixels of the left part lighten

furTufts.does: fur along a sprite's back: in every third column the outline lifts a pixel where it is the top edge, not on the face
furTufts.purpose: a furry back whose edge is tufted rather than smooth, anchored to the body

inspiration.text: hatching: texture from a regular pattern of marks

furTufts.inWords: In each column where (column + anchor) is a multiple of 3 and not within 1.48 face radii of the face, find the top pixel; if it is the outline and the pixel under it is filled with another colour, the outline moves up a pixel and the old place takes the colour under it.
tests: the outline lifts a pixel in every third column, never on the face

rimDetail.does: the detail a sprite drawn finer can hold, levels 2 to 4: a lit top rim and a shaded underside, fur strokes and scale highlights, then denser and speckled
rimDetail.purpose: creatures that gain detail with the pixels to hold it, rather than the same drawing blown up

inspiration.text: cel shading: a lit band and a shaded band
hatching: strokes in a regular pattern

rimDetail.inWords: Level 1 changes nothing. A pixel with empty space within the rim above it (1 deep, 2 from level 3) lightens by 1.1 steps; else with empty space within the rim plus one below it darkens by 0.75. From level 3, fur pixels on a grid (4 by 3, 3 by 2 at level 4) darken by 0.9 with the pixel down and back of them, and scale pixels on odd rows where (column + 2 when the row's half is odd + 301) is a multiple of 3 lighten by 0.7. At level 4, pixels where (7 column + 13 row) is a multiple of 23 become the speckle colour.
tests: at level 1 it changes nothing; from level 2 the top edge lightens and the underside darkens

smoothCurve.does: n values along a body from a few given places, each eased between the two it falls between
smoothCurve.purpose: a body's widths and heights from head to tail with no kinks, from a handful of numbers

inspiration.text: smoothstep easing between two values

smoothCurve.inWords: Value i is at u = i / (n - 1). Find the two given places u falls between; t is how far between them (clamped to 0..1); the value is the first plus the difference times 3t^2 - 2t^3.
tests: it passes through the values it is given, eased between them

bodySpots.does: spots along a body: each on a part in a range, off its middle a little, of a size, in the main colour or the second
bodySpots.purpose: markings that make individuals of a species, drawn from a seed

inspiration.text: animals' spots: scattered unevenly, some in a second colour

bodySpots.inWords: For each spot: a part from first to last, an offset across of -0.55..0.45 and along of -0.5..0.2 of the part's radius, a size of 0.5..0.9 of it, and the second colour with a chance of 0.3, drawn in that order.
tests: every spot is on a part in its range, and the same seed gives the same spots

bodyPattern.does: a body's pattern picked from the kinds allowed: none, bands, a saddle over the back, a tail tip, or the back only
bodyPattern.purpose: a family of pattern kinds that each body plan narrows to its own

inspiration.text: animals' markings: banded, saddled, tipped tails, darker backs

bodyPattern.inWords: Pick a kind. Bands are every 2nd or 3rd part from a phase of 0..2; a saddle runs from part 2 to 45 per cent of the body (at least 3); a tip covers the last 2..4 parts.
tests: it is always one of the kinds it is allowed

coatColours.does: a coat's three packed colours: a back near a hue, a paler less saturated belly, an accent turned round the colour wheel
coatColours.purpose: animals of one land in colours that belong together, each still its own

inspiration.text: hue, saturation and lightness
tints: a colour mixed toward white

coatColours.inWords: The hue is the one given (or random) plus up to its spread (25 if none) either way; saturation 0.35..0.6 and lightness 0.42..0.6 unless the kind gives its own. The accent turns the hue by the kind's turn or one of 150, 180, 30, -30, 60, -60, 120, plus up to 15 either way, a little more saturated and lighter; the belly turns 10..35, at 0.45 of the saturation and 0.26 lighter (0.6..0.9).
tests: the back stays near the hue asked for, and the belly is paler than the back

blendRecords.does: two records mixed: numbers between, other values the nearer side's, records within records the same way; one only one side has fades out by its sizes
blendRecords.purpose: two creatures' genomes mixed part for part, so any blend of two bodies is still a body

inspiration.text: linear interpolation

blendRecords.inWords: If both have a key: two numbers mix at t, two records mix the same way, anything else is a's below half way and b's from it. If one side is missing, the other's sizes (keys matching len, h, span, fan, r, rx, ry) are scaled by how much of it is left, and it is gone below 0.08.
tests: numbers mix, other values switch at half way, and a part only one side has shrinks away

cloudShadows.does: the shadows of clouds over a frame seen from above: a bent fractal noise read on a coarse grid and smoothed between, darkening the land where it is high
cloudShadows.purpose: weather a land shows without a sky in the picture: clouds known only by their shadows drifting over the ground with the wind

inspiration.text: fractal noise for a cloud cover, its heights cut by a threshold
a slow field read on a coarse grid and smoothed between its points, so each pixel costs a few multiplications
a cloud's shadow on a field is a little blue, and soft at its edge

cloudShadows.inWords: The noise is read every 8 pixels over the frame and a cell more each way, its inputs bent by sines so the clouds come out round, and smoothed between. Where it is above a height set by how much of the sky is cloud, the pixel is darkened (red and green to 82%, blue to 90%); just above that height only every other pixel is, for a soft edge; in weak light only half the pixels are.
tests: it only ever darkens: no channel of any pixel goes up, and blue keeps more of its value than red and green
more cloud cover darkens more of the frame

fogBanks.does: banks of fog over a frame: a slow bent fractal noise says where it is thick or thin; thick fog laid over the land, middling fog in an ordered dither, thin fog as a faint veil
fogBanks.purpose: fog that drifts in banks and lets the land show through evenly where it is thin, in a pixel picture

inspiration.text: fractal noise for where the fog is thick
a slow field read on a coarse grid and smoothed between its points
an even ordered dither for a share of cover, where lines would read as scratches

fogBanks.inWords: The noise is read every 8 pixels and smoothed between. Its value, with the density, gives a cover: none, nothing changes; full, the fog colour is mixed in at 86%; between, pixels the 4 by 4 Bayer matrix lets through take it at 74%, and the rest, where the cover is above 0.3, at 22%.
tests: denser fog changes more of the frame, and every changed pixel moves toward the fog's colour

frontStrength.does: how strong a passing front of rain or snow is at a moment: building over its first seconds, full through its middle, easing off at its end
frontStrength.purpose: rain that comes and goes as a front, without a step-by-step state to keep

inspiration.text: a smoothstep in, a smoothstep out

frontStrength.inWords: A smoothstep from 4 to 14 seconds after the front comes, times one less a smoothstep over its last 9 seconds.
tests: it is 0 when the front comes, 1 through its middle, and 0 again at its end

lightningFlash.does: the whole frame lit for an instant, twice, as a flash flickers: full, dark, full again, then faintly as it fades, each channel drawn toward a cold white
lightningFlash.purpose: a storm's lightning in a picture seen from above, where the bolt itself is out of sight

inspiration.text: lightning seen from the ground lights everything in a quick double flicker, cold and blue-white

lightningFlash.inWords: With 0.34 seconds of flash left it is full until 0.26, dark until 0.18, full again until 0.1, and at a third after that. Lit, red is drawn 60% of the way to white times the level, green 62%, blue 70%.
tests: it lights the frame, then not, then again, then faintly, as the flash runs out
a lit pixel only grows brighter, blue the most

hourLight.does: the hour's light as how much it is night, how much it is the low light of dusk or dawn, whether it is morning, and a key that says when its colour tables must be made again
hourLight.purpose: a day's light that grades a whole pixel picture cheaply: tables made only when the light has really changed

inspiration.text: colour grading by the hour

hourLight.inWords: The sun's height is the cosine of the time from noon. Night grows as it sinks past a little below the horizon; the low light is strongest with the sun at the horizon, less at night. The key rounds them to 24ths (the shade to 40ths, the wet to tenths); the plain day's key needs no grading.
tests: noon is plain day and midnight is full night

hourTables.does: the hour as three colour tables, one a channel: night sinking to a deep blue, evening warming the lights a little and lifting the shadows into violet, dawn cooler and paler
hourTables.purpose: a whole frame graded by the hour with three table lookups a pixel

inspiration.text: colour grading by curves, a channel each
a curve kept as a table of 256 values
evening light warms what it lights and turns shadows violet; a plain multiply turns snow peach

hourTables.inWords: Each channel is scaled (at full night red to 34%, green to 43%, blue to 72%) and lifted a little at night; the low light warms red, cools green and blue, and adds violet to the shadows (more to darker values), less at dawn; shade and wet air scale it down a little more.
tests: at full night a mid grey keeps more of its blue than its green, and more of its green than its red

gradeFrame.does: a frame graded by the hour's tables, with lamps holding off the dark round themselves in steps, dithered at their edges
gradeFrame.purpose: night over a pixel world with lit windows, lanterns and the player's own light, at a lookup a pixel

inspiration.text: colour grading by tables
light in steps, dithered at their edges

gradeFrame.inWords: With no lamps (or by day) every pixel is looked up in the tables. Otherwise each lamp marks how much it holds the dark off over its own reach (an ellipse 1.5 times as wide as tall, falling off with the square of the distance); where that is above 0.02 the graded colour is drawn back toward the ungraded one by that much, in sixths, with a small pattern dithering the steps, and never more than 85% of the way.
tests: a lamp keeps the colours near it closer to the ungraded ones than those far from it

fleeVector.does: which way to run from threats: each threat in its reach pushes away from itself, harder the nearer it is, the pushes added, and how long the fear lasts
fleeVector.purpose: animals that scatter from what comes too near, many threats at once

inspiration.text: flee, a steering behaviour

fleeVector.inWords: For each threat nearer than its reach, the offset from it divided by its length plus a tenth is added up. The fear is 1.2 seconds, or 2.2 for a hard threat, the most of those in reach.
tests: a threat in reach pushes directly away from it, and one out of reach does nothing

formationSlot.does: a follower's place beside its leader: round it in a loose flock, trailing behind it in a school, or in a V behind it
formationSlot.purpose: groups of animals that keep together in their own manner, each follower steering for a place of its own

inspiration.text: flocking, and following a leader as a steering behaviour
geese fly in a V; fish trail behind a leader; grazing animals spread round one

formationSlot.inWords: A loose flock: each place at an angle 2.4 radians on from the last, 7 to 19 away by fours, squashed to 0.8 north to south. A school: behind the leader along its heading, 3 plus 1.6 a follower back, a little to one side. A V: followers alternately to each side, each pair 7 further back and spread 0.7 as wide.
tests: a vee puts followers alternately to each side, each pair further back

wobbledRing.does: how far a point is past the edge of a round world whose edge is pushed in and out by a broad and a fine noise
wobbledRing.purpose: a finite world whose edge reads as a coast or a mountain wall, not a ring

inspiration.text: a circle's radius pushed by value noise

wobbledRing.inWords: The distance from the middle less the radius, the radius pushed by a broad value noise (up to 17% of it each way) and a fine one (up to 5 each way).
tests: far inside it is negative and far outside positive, and the edge stays within the wobble of the circle

mountainRise.does: how high a mountain wall stands at a point past a world's edge: rising from just inside it to full height further out, broken by ridged noise
mountainRise.purpose: mountains that close a bounded world, standing as a range, not a ramp

inspiration.text: ridged noise for mountain ranges

mountainRise.inWords: Rising in a straight line from 6 inside the edge to 110 past it, times 0.55 plus 0.45 of a ridged noise.
tests: it is 0 well inside the edge and rises past it, never above 1

windingRiver.does: a river that winds across a land: where a slow fractal noise crosses its middle value, one unbroken winding line, as wide as its level asks
windingRiver.purpose: rivers in a world made from noise, running on without a path drawn for them

inspiration.text: a contour of fractal noise as a winding line

windingRiver.inWords: The noise, read slowly, is measured from its middle value as a band 0..1; within a fifth of the level of the middle it is river, deepest on the line itself.
tests: more of a land is river the higher its level

plotGrid.does: plots in a grid laid at an angle, such as paddy fields or salt pans: which plot a point is in, and how far it is from that plot's nearest edge
plotGrid.purpose: fields in plots with a bank round each, not lined up with the picture

inspiration.text: a point turned into the grid's frame

plotGrid.inWords: The point is turned by the grid's angle, then divided into plots of the size given; the distance to the nearest edge is the least of the four.
tests: every point is within half a plot of its plot's edge, and at angle 0 the plots are squares lined up with the picture

nearestFreeCell.does: the open cell nearest a cell: itself if open, else the first open one on rings drawn outward
nearestFreeCell.purpose: a walker asked to go somewhere it cannot stand (inside a wall, out on the water) goes to the nearest place it can

inspiration.text: A* needs its start and goal on open cells

nearestFreeCell.inWords: If the cell is open, it is the answer. Otherwise look at the rings round it, one cell further each time: for each ring, across it, the cell on its top row, its bottom row, its left side and its right side, and answer with the first open one. Past the last ring asked for, there is none.
tests: it answers the cell itself when open, else an open cell on the nearest ring

roofPlan.does: a gable or hip roof seen from above, from its foot: the eaves' rectangle, the ridge's row a little above the middle (three tenths back from the north eave), and how far a hip roof's ends slope in
roofPlan.purpose: pixel-art houses whose roofs read as raised and sloping from straight above, the ridge where the eye expects it

inspiration.text: gable and hip roofs, and eaves reaching past the walls

roofPlan.inWords: The roof is the walls' width and depth plus the eave on every side, centred on the foot's x, its south eave on the foot's row and its north eave the roof's depth above. The ridge sits three tenths of the way down from the north eave (it is raised, so it shows above the middle). A hip roof's ends slope in by 0.42 of the depth; a gable's do not.
tests: its ridge lies between its eaves, nearer the north one, and only a hip roof's ends slope in

slopeShade.does: how a roof's near slope shades at a row: dark along the eave, lit just under the ridge, else its own colour
slopeShade.purpose: a slope that reads as tilted toward the light at the top and into shadow at the eave, with two tones only

inspiration.text: the shadow an eave casts, and light catching the top of a slope

slopeShade.inWords: Measure the row's place from the ridge (0) to the eave (1). Past four fifths it is the eave's shadow; before one sixth it is lit under the ridge; anywhere else, nothing changes.
tests: the rows just under the ridge are lit, the last rows by the eave are dark, and the middle is left as it is

roofTexel.does: a roof covering's texture at a pixel: tiles in staggered rows (or in mortar), thatch in ragged layers, boards with nails, lacquered boards, each as a word the caller colours
roofTexel.purpose: roof coverings that read at a few pixels a tile, the same pattern on every roof of a kind, laid only on the roof's own pixels

inspiration.text: roofs of overlapping tiles in staggered courses, and thatch laid in layers

roofTexel.inWords: Rows run parallel to the eave from the slope's corner. Tiles: rows four deep, tiles six wide, each row moved three along; a seam under every row and at every joint (mortar for red tiles), a lit pixel beside the joint in a row's top half, the third row of plain tiles a little shaded. Thatch: layers five deep whose lower edge is dark except where a hash leaves a gap, light straws on a layer's top row and dark gaps and pale straws by the same hash. Boards: six wide, a dark seam and a lit edge, a nail every nine rows. Lacquered boards: a dark line every four across and a shaded line every seven down.
tests: tiles repeat every six pixels across and four down, their rows staggered by three
red tiles show mortar where plain tiles show a dark seam

obliqueToGround.does: the point of the ground under a place in the oblique view: worked out as if the ground were flat, then once more at the height found there
obliqueToGround.purpose: a click or a tap on a picture with heights lands on the ground the player sees there, not the flat ground behind it

inspiration.text: inverting an oblique projection, with one correction for the height

obliqueToGround.inWords: Take the place as if on flat ground: its depth is how far down it is, its offset across is how far across less m times that depth. Ask the ground's height there, add it to the depth (a raised point shows higher) and work out the offset across again.
tests: it undoes obliqueToScreen, on flat ground and on a raised step

wallShade.does: a wall's lightness at a texel of a 16-pixel tile by its stuff: a lit top edge, then stone in courses with mortar, earth in bands with grit, snow in drifts, sand with grains
wallShade.purpose: terrace walls that say what they are made of at a glance, in lightness only so one tile takes any ground's colour

inspiration.text: masonry laid in courses, each course's joints set off from the one below

wallShade.inWords: The top row is the lit edge (1.0). Stone: courses five rows deep, the blocks eight wide, every other course moved four along; the mortar (the fifth row of a course and the last column of a block) dark, a block's face a little lighter or darker by a hash and darker toward its foot. Earth: bands three rows deep in two tones, grit specks by a hash, the row under the edge a little lighter. Snow: the top two rows bright, the rest with soft drifts by a coarse hash. Sand: grains by a hash, a little darker below the tenth row.
tests: each stuff's top row is the lit edge, and stone's mortar runs in courses of five with joints every eight, staggered

leafShade.does: leaves' lightness at a texel: light ones in small heaps, a few dark gaps between, the rest a little uneven
leafShade.purpose: clumps of leaves with a texture of their own, so a crown of plain balls still reads as foliage

inspiration.text: texture laid on a lit surface to suggest detail the geometry does not have

leafShade.inWords: A hash of the texel's place in two-by-two blocks: above 0.72 a heap of light leaves (1.12), below 0.16 a gap (0.7), else 0.94 moved a little by a finer hash.
tests: its values are heaps of light, gaps of dark and a narrow middle, nothing else

crownRows.does: a tree sprite's crown: its rows above the trunk (the narrow part going up from the foot), each row's opaque span
crownRows.purpose: the crown of a drawn tree, found from the drawing alone, so it can be stood up, lit and shadowed as a body while its trunk stays a post

inspiration.text: reading a shape from a sprite's opaque pixels

crownRows.inWords: Find the first row with any opaque pixel. From the foot row go up while the row's opaque span is under five pixels wide: that is the trunk. Every row from the top to there with an opaque pixel is the crown, with its first and last opaque columns.
tests: a lollipop sprite's crown is its round top and its trunk the narrow stick

silhouetteNormals.does: a normal map made from a sprite's own silhouette: a crown as a ball lit from the upper left, its drawn clumps raised and sunk; a trunk round; a lump as a dome; anything else a card turned a little up
silhouetteNormals.purpose: pixel-art sprites stood up in a lit 3D scene that keep their drawn look but take light and shadow like bodies

inspiration.text: normal maps: a surface's facing stored per texel, lighting detail the geometry does not have

silhouetteNormals.inWords: Fit an ellipse to the crown's rows (or, for a lump, a half ellipse standing on its foot). Each pixel in it faces out of the ellipse at its place, tipped a little up, and leans away from its lighter neighbours (light is raised, dark sunk). A trunk's pixel faces out of its row's width. Everything else faces the eye, a little up. Each normal is made length one and stored as bytes, green counting down the rows.
tests: a crown faces up and left at its upper left and down and right at its lower right; a card faces the eye everywhere
